Subject: Re: Relaying Denied

Dennis Putnam wrote:
>>
>> mail for aimaudit.biz loops "back to myself". most probably, the MX 
>> for this domain is set to your postfix box, but postfix was not 
>> configured to serve this domain. either list the domain in 
>> mydestination or virtual_mailbox_domains, or set a transport entry to 
>> forward the mail to the right server... etc.
>
> I thought that is what 'mydestination' does (although I don't need 
> that on my primary server so the defaults must be sufficient there). 

it is recommended to set mydestination, myhostname and mydomain 
explicitely to avoid surprises. you don't want to ruin your mail setup 
whenever you play with the system hostname... etc.

> As I said I must be missing something fundamental and everyone here is 
> giving me more credit then I am due thus overlooking potential stupid 
> mistakes. I think this is related to the MX records but I want to 
> somehow get this configured so I can test without changing my DNS.
>
>>
>>>
>>> Here is the log for a non-local account (unfortunately I don't have 
>>> a way to test this from here using a different domain which might be 
>>> more helpful):
>>>
>>> Feb 20 12:14:59 xserveone postfix/smtp[22856]: 722B1499A56: 
>>> to=, relay=127.0.0.1[127.0.0.1], delay=47, 
>>> status=sent (250 2.5.0 Ok, id=21649-01, BOUNCE)
>>
>> your content filter said: 250 ... BOUNCE. postfix successfully 
>> delivered the message.
>
> Not my content filter, that of the recipient's server.

No, it's 127.0.0.1. so it's running on the same box.


====

Dennis Putnam wrote:
 > The problem is solved. Out of desperation, I decided to reboot the 
server.
 > Somehow that must have reloaded some configuration from somewhere 
that 'postfix reload' did not.
 > I have no clue as to what it could have been.

probably an IP configuration change. next time, try restarting postfix 
before rebooting the box.
